title: American Art
description: From frontier light to mid-century city scenes — the American eye.

items.title: The Gulf Stream
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor and traces of blotting, over graphite, on moderately thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper (lower edge trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Gulf Stream' depicts a lone man adrift in a dismasted sailboat, surrounded by circling sharks on a turbulent sea. Executed primarily in transparent watercolor, this work vividly captures a dramatic struggle for survival against the forces of nature.
items.tags: maritime, survival, nature, realism, watercolor, dramatic, American art

items.title: The Herring Net
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Herring Net' depicts two fishermen hauling in a net teeming with fish, their small dory battling the choppy waters of the open sea. The dynamic composition and raw portrayal capture the arduous labor and natural forces faced by those working the maritime environment.
items.tags: maritime, realism, american art, fishing, labor, ocean, 19th century

items.title: After the Hurricane, Bahamas
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on moderately thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the raw aftermath of a devastating storm in the Bahamas, depicting a lone figure surveying the wreckage on a desolate shore. Executed primarily in transparent watercolor, the work showcases Homer's skill in rendering light, atmosphere, and the enduring power of nature.
items.tags: hurricane, bahamas, seascape, aftermath, watercolor, realism, solitude, 19th century

items.title: Croquet Scene
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Croquet Scene' captures a moment of leisure in 19th-century America, depicting figures engaged in the popular lawn game. Painted in 1866, this oil on canvas work reflects the changing social customs and outdoor pursuits of the post-Civil War era.
items.tags: croquet, leisure, social scene, 19th century, American art, genre painting, Winslow Homer, realism

items.title: The Water Fan
items.medium: Watercolor, with blotting and touches of scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough twill-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Water Fan' captures the dynamic interplay of light and water with remarkable immediacy, utilizing the unique properties of watercolor. This evocative work demonstrates Homer's mastery in depicting the power and subtle beauty of the natural world.
items.tags: watercolor, seascape, ocean, nature, American art, late 19th century, realism

items.title: Life-Size Black Bass
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper (left, right and lower edges trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Life-Size Black Bass' vividly portrays the aquatic subject using transparent watercolor. Created in 1904, this artwork showcases the artist's distinctive ability to capture nature with striking immediacy.
items.tags: fish, bass, wildlife, watercolor, realism, nature, american art

items.title: Stowing Sail
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting, scraping and graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the dynamic energy of mariners at sea as they prepare a vessel's sails. His command of transparent watercolor is evident in this vivid maritime scene.
items.tags: maritime, sailing, watercolor, american art, sea, labor, early 20th century

items.title: North Woods Club, Adirondacks (The Interrupted Tete-a-Tete)
items.medium: Watercolor, with rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'North Woods Club, Adirondacks' captures a scene from the wilderness, its subtitle suggesting an 'interrupted tête-à-tête' within nature. Created in watercolor with techniques like rewetting and scraping, the work demonstrates Homer's skill in depicting the rugged beauty of the Adirondacks.
items.tags: adirondacks, nature, wilderness, watercolor, american art, 19th century, realism

items.title: Mount Washington
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "Mount Washington" captures the majestic presence of New Hampshire's highest peak. This painting exemplifies Homer's keen observation of the American landscape and its natural grandeur.
items.tags: mountain, landscape, nature, american art, realism, grandeur, new england

items.title: Peach Blossoms
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting, titled "Peach Blossoms," was created by American artist Winslow Homer in 1878. It depicts the delicate beauty of peach blossoms, a common subject in nature-focused art.
items.tags: landscape, nature, american art, 19th century, realism, painting

items.title: Coast of Maine
items.description_narrative: This powerful oil painting by Winslow Homer captures the rugged grandeur of the Maine coastline, a frequent subject for the artist in his later career. Depicting turbulent waters crashing against stark rock formations, it embodies his masterful portrayal of nature's raw power and isolation.
items.tags: maine, coastline, ocean, realism, american art, landscape, marine art, nature

items.title: Breaking Storm, Coast of Maine
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and traces of scraping, on thick, rough-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "Breaking Storm, Coast of Maine" vividly captures the raw power of nature as a tempestuous sea crashes against a rugged shore. Executed in 1894, this watercolor employs transparent and opaque pigments, rewetting, and scraping to convey the dynamic atmospheric effects of an approaching storm.
items.tags: seascape, storm, marine art, watercolor, realism, American art, late 19th century

items.title: For to Be a Farmer's Boy
items.medium: Transparent and opaque watercolor, with rewetting, blotting, and scraping, heightened with gum glaze, over graphite, on thick, rough-textured ivory wove paper (lower edge trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'For to Be a Farmer's Boy,' created in 1887, exemplifies his innovative approach to watercolor. The artist masterfully employs transparent and opaque pigments, rewetting, blotting, and scraping techniques, heightened with gum glaze, on thick, rough-textured ivory wove paper.
items.tags: american art, watercolor, rural life, realism, 19th century, genre scene

items.title: The Rapids, Hudson River, Adirondacks
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with traces of opaque watercolor, blotting, and scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the dynamic power of nature in 'The Rapids, Hudson River, Adirondacks,' showcasing rushing water and rugged terrain. Executed in transparent watercolor, with subtle touches of opaque watercolor and scraping, the work demonstrates Homer's profound connection to the American wilderness.
items.tags: watercolor, landscape, american art, nature, realism, hudson river, adirondacks

items.title: The Fountain, Villa Torlonia, Frascati, Italy
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the grand fountain at Villa Torlonia in Frascati, Italy. The artwork masterfully renders the play of light and shadow across the water and surrounding classical architecture.
items.tags: landscape, Italy, fountain, villa, oil painting, light, Edwardian, architecture

items.title: Mrs. George Swinton (Elizabeth Ebsworth)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1897 portrait of Mrs. George Swinton captures her elegant pose and sophisticated attire. This oil on canvas exemplifies Sargent's mastery of society portraiture and his distinctive brushwork.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, society portraiture, gilded age, elegance, late 19th century, realism, london society

items.title: Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's oil on canvas portrait of Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre) captures the sitter with characteristic elegance and directness. Painted in 1882, the work exemplifies Sargent's mastery of light and texture in rendering a commanding social presence.
items.tags: portrait, woman, society portraiture, realism, elegant, 19th century, american art

items.title: Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 'Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)' captures a moment of quiet observation through the artist's masterful brushwork. Executed in 1891, this oil on canvas work exemplifies Sargent's ability to render the human form with both immediacy and profound dignity.
items.tags: portrait, life study, egyptian, female figure, oil painting, john singer sargent, realism, late 19th century

items.title: Venetian Glass Workers
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the intense labor and vibrant atmosphere of a glass-blowing workshop in Venice. The painting showcases the dynamic interplay of light and shadow on the workers and their fiery craft.
items.tags: venetian, glassblowing, workers, genre scene, realism, industrial, light, craftsmanship

items.title: Thistles
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 'Thistles' offers a detailed study of the plant, rendered in oil on canvas. Painted between 1883 and 1889, this work exemplifies the artist's expressive brushwork and keen observation of nature.
items.tags: thistles, botanical study, nature, oil painting, american art, late 19th century
